item.title: Hayden Panettiere’s mom discloses heartbreaking ultimatum in their final phone call before actress’ death
item.description: Hayden Panettiere's mom reveals the therapist-advised ultimatum over Brian Hickerson that led to their estrangement months before the actress' death.
item.content:encoded:
Hayden Panettiere's mom is detailing the heartbreaking ultimatum that led to their estrangement months before the actress' death.

In an interview with "Good Morning America," which aired Monday, Lesley Vogel said she and the late actress had become estranged in the months before Panettiere's death after Vogel gave her daughter an ultimatum over her daughter's relationship with on-again, off-again boyfriend Brian Hickerson.

About a year ago, Vogel traveled to California to stay with Panettiere and help her end her relationship with Hickerson — a decision the "Nashville" star made on her own, Vogel claimed.

HAYDEN PANETTIERE'S MOTHER POINTS FINGER AT BRIAN HICKERSON AFTER 'NASHVILLE' STAR'S DEATH AT 36

"She knew that Brian was toxic," Vogel said. "She knew she had to get him out of her life."

Vogel said things began to change after about six weeks, when she noticed her daughter slowly pulling away. It was then that she returned home to Florida.

HAYDEN PANETTIERE AND THE CHILD STARS WHOSE RELATIONSHIPS WITH THEIR MOMAGERS TURNED COMPLICATED

"When I got the phone call from her saying, ‘I’m going to be with the person I love,’ … I just lost it," Vogel recalled. "I could not believe that she had gone that far back, that he had been successful in reeling her back in with all of the things he had done to her."

Vogel said that, on the advice of her therapist, she told Panettiere that she could no longer speak with her as long as Hickerson remained part of her life.

The decision marked the beginning of their estrangement — something Vogel believed would only be temporary.

"I needed to have that pocket of time," she said. "Of course, I thought it was going to be a pocket of time. I did not by any stretch of the imagination think that this was going to happen to Hayden."

"I don’t know why, I just didn’t," she added. "Maybe I didn’t want to."

Panettiere was found dead inside a Greenville, South Carolina residence on Aug. 16.

POLICE SHOW UP AT HOME LINKED TO HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S ON-AND-OFF BOYFRIEND DAYS AFTER HER SUDDEN DEATH

Hickerson and his brother, Zach, called 911 after finding the actress unresponsive, according to a police report obtained by Fox News Digital. Hickerson later gave authorities a bag containing medication Panettiere had been taking, according to the report.

Preliminary autopsy results found no signs of trauma that contributed to Panettiere’s death, the Greenville County Coroner's Office confirmed to Fox News Digital. However, Panettiere's death remains under investigation.

HAYDEN PANETTIERE REMEMBERED BY VIOLA DAVIS, BETHANY JOY LENZ AND OTHER CELEBRITIES AFTER SUDDEN DEATH AT 36

Fox News has learned the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) has also been contacted and is assisting with the investigation.

Vogel told "GMA" that Panettiere lived a very "happy life" until her late teens.

DISNEY ALUM CHRISTY CARLSON ROMANO RIPS HOLLYWOOD FOR FAILING CHILD STARS AFTER HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S DEATH

"I would say at about 17, I started seeing her going downhill," Vogel said. "As she got older, and it wasn’t my voice anymore. I wasn’t in charge of her choices."

Panettiere's decision to give up custody of her daughter, Kaya — whom she shared with former fiancé Wladimir Klitschko — was a turning point, Vogel said.

HAYDEN PANETTIERE DEFENDS GIVING UP CUSTODY OF HER DAUGHTER DESPITE INTENSE 'EMOTIONAL PAIN'

"Vlad had taken over custody, you know, for safety," Vogel said. "In my opinion, that was the catalyst that she just couldn’t keep those demons away."

In an interview with the New York Times, Vogel said her daughter was living with chronic physical pain.

"She was in pain," Vogel said. "She was afraid. She couldn’t physically function properly."

Vogel said she brought Panettiere to multiple doctors and pursued massage and acupuncture treatments to address the "pins and needles" sensation the actress often experienced in her lower extremities.

Ultimately, Vogel said, she hopes her daughter will be remembered for the "talented, beautiful, outgoing, intelligent woman" she was.

"She really was," Vogel told "GMA". "But I also want people to understand that it is my belief that she was suffering. Now that doesn't make sense because when you look at a beautiful girl who's got an incredible career, even though it has had its ups and downs, but, you look at that big picture, and you go, 'Why would you be suffering?' People don't understand that you can have, on the exterior, all of this, but that doesn't mean that what's going on in here matches."

item.title: Mamdani jumps into Democratic Party feud, alleging boss seeking to subvert 'will of voters'
item.description: Zohran Mamdani opposes Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn's push to add voting members to the Brooklyn Democratic Party executive committee before a fall vote.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is opposing a last-minute push to overhaul Brooklyn Democratic Party rules, arguing the proposed changes would undermine voters after reformers made gains in the June primary.

"I very much oppose these proposed changes, by the current Brooklyn Democratic Party chair," Mamdani said. "I oppose them because they are an attempt to circumnavigate the will of voters."

The proposals from Brooklyn Democratic Party chair Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn would add more than two dozen voting members to the party’s executive committee, which will choose the party chair this fall, after a slate of reformers won 22 district leader seats in the June primary, according to the City Reporter.

NYC TAXPAYERS COULD PAY TWICE UNDER MAMDANI'S CITY-OWNED GROCERY STORE PLAN

The newly elected district leaders will not take their seats until the fall, and Bichotte Hermelyn and her supporters still hold a majority as current district leaders prepare to vote on the proposed changes Tuesday night, according to the outlet.

Bichotte Hermelyn has described the changes as an effort to broaden participation in the party.

"We want to create a perception of inclusiveness," she told NY1. In a video released by the Brooklyn Democratic organization, she said the proposals would "expand leadership" and "expand representation."

The reformers have backed longtime Sunset Park district leader Julio Peña to become the next party chair. If the proposed changes pass, the additional voting members would take part in the fall leadership election.

VICE PRESIDENT JD VANCE BLASTS MAMDANI, EL-SAYED, AOC AND OSSOFF IN RAPID-FIRE TIKTOK ROAST

Mamdani said the Brooklyn Democratic Party should reflect what New Yorkers want, rather than the kind of politics that has left people "disengaged and disaffected with politics at large."

New York Attorney General Letitia James and Public Advocate Jumaane Williams have also urged the party not to move forward with the changes.

"New Yorkers deserve leaders who are committed to serving their communities, not rewriting rules to hold onto power," they said in a joint statement obtained by City and State New York. "Changing the makeup of an executive committee on the eve of a leadership vote goes against what we believe in as Democrats and should not move forward."

Another proposal would give former party chairs a vote in future leadership elections even after they are no longer district leaders.

According to the City Reporter, that appears to mean former party chair Clarence Norman could vote on future party leadership. Norman resigned in 2005 after multiple corruption convictions, including one for soliciting bribes from judicial nominees.

After the leadership election, another proposed change would allow additional voting members to be appointed from each Assembly district, potentially bringing the executive committee to about 90 members.

item.title: Reporter's Notebook: College sports bill enters legislative 'red zone' as season kicks off
item.description: As North Carolina and Texas Christian open the season in Dublin, the Senate's bipartisan college sports bill stalls amid disputes over NIL rules.
item.content:encoded:
The college football season kicks off this Saturday with North Carolina playing Texas Christian University in Dublin, Ireland.

This marks the start of a sprint until early April when college football and basketball practically compete on a near-daily basis with MLB, the NFL, the NBA and NHL.

This college football season begins with lawmakers falling short of a goal to pass a bill to alter the flow of money in college sports. And despite recent momentum, lawmakers may be lucky to pass the bill when the clock shows zeroes on April 5 in Detroit and the NCAA crowns its next basketball Final Four champion.

PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT STALLS IN OVERNIGHT SENATE SHOWDOWN, VOTE PUSHED TO SEPTEMBER AFTER CHAOTIC EVENING

President Trump demanded that the Senate stay in session this month to pass a bipartisan college sports measure. That wasn’t going to happen simply because the bill’s not ready yet. The measure didn’t even secure a specific agreement for a test vote when the Senate returns in September. Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, said there was a deal for a vote at some point. However, an unrelated bill to regulate cryptocurrency marshaled a concrete time for a test vote on the afternoon of Tuesday, Sept. 15. The college sports measure didn’t head into the August recess with that level of certainty.

But the one thing that is certain? Intercollegiate athletics face myriad problems.

"College sports right now is in crisis. It is chaos that is ripping college sports apart," said Cruz.

"I think that the arms race that exists now where people are just paying any amount of money from a system is not the right way to get this done," said Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash. She’s the top Democrat on the Senate Commerce Committee and helped craft the bipartisan legislation with Cruz.

CLOCK IS TICKING AS SENATORS TED CRUZ, MARIA CANTWELL PUSH FOR SEC, BIG TEN BUY-IN ON COLLEGE SPORTS BILL

The measure establishes a national standard for athlete compensation — including NIL — for the use of name, image and likeness of athletes. It also limits them to one transfer without losing eligibility within a five-year window.

But understanding the bill’s remedies is challenging.

"[The bill] seemed pretty dense when I read it," yours truly observed to Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., one afternoon in a hallway of the Dirksen Senate Office Building.

"It's dense as hell," replied Kennedy. "And that’s a legal term."

The measure raises the ceiling of money schools can use to compensate athletes. It essentially allows "third-party entities," like athletic footwear or equipment manufacturers like Under Armour or Nike, to pipeline additional money to schools.

Naturally, football and men’s basketball score most of the money under the current system. But lawmakers worry that women’s athletics and smaller sports like volleyball, lacrosse and soccer could evaporate unless Congress intervenes.

"It's the revenue from football and maybe basketball, but mostly football that funds everything else," said Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del.

The college sports bill seemed to gain traction in late July when the Big Ten and SEC — the most muscular of all college athletic conferences — announced their support of the legislation. Lawmakers could try to write a bill all they wanted, but with all due respect to the Mid-American Conference and Mountain West, the measure wouldn’t go anywhere unless the Big Ten and SEC were on board.

It was thought that the college sports package might get a test vote before the August recess, but a band of conservatives claimed the legislation fell short when it came to protecting women from competing against men.

"It looks like a bunch of trial lawyers drew this thing up," said Sen. Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., a former Division I football coach who ran programs at Ole Miss, Auburn, Texas Tech and Cincinnati.

UNIVERSITIES ARE DESPERATE TO WIN NOW, BUT ATHLETES AND THE NATION BOTH LOSE

Tuberville teamed up with Sens. Jim Banks, R-Ind., and Josh Hawley, R-Mo., to craft an amendment going further in the legislation. Banks believed that the bill could undercut Indiana state law, which extends prohibitions on biological males competing in K-12 sports to college athletics. Banks expressed concern that the Cruz/Cantwell bill "would preempt Indiana’s law." The Indiana Republican asserted that he couldn’t support the legislation as written.

However, President Donald Trump torched those who said the bill failed to bar men from playing women’s sports at any level.

"Nobody has done more to protect Women Athletes than me — and this Bill CLEARLY protects the Laws in 27 States protecting Women's Sports, and banning Men from Women's Sports. Anyone who tells you differently is LYING!" thundered the president on Truth Social.

Trump worried that without adoption of this legislation, "Programs will be canceled, Women's and Olympic Sports will go away, the fans will be robbed, and Universities will go broke." He then asked the Senate to "stay in D.C. until it passes."

Despite the president’s advocacy, that wasn’t going to happen. However, the legislation does have a new set of downs — thanks to the Big Ten and SEC.

The Congressional Black Caucus (CBC) opposes the bill. In a statement, the CBC said the package fails to incorporate "perspectives of Black athletes."

Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., is the only former Division I football player in the Senate, competing as a tight end for Stanford. He opposes the bill.

"There are a lot of people who have substantive objections with that bill that should give us all pause," said Booker.

THE "PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT" HAS A FATAL FLAW: IT DOESN’T PROTECT WOMEN | RILEY GAINES

So the Senate essentially took a timeout on the bill with the August recess. As any fan knows, timeouts are essential in sports. They allow teams to regroup. Rehydrate with water or Gatorade. Players to catch their breath. Coaches to draw up a special play to bring the team to victory.

It’s not known what the play call might be from Cruz, Cantwell or even Trump. Or if anything would work. Some skeptics believe the Senate’s decision to leave Washington without the locked-in test vote could cost the bill momentum — compared to the deal dictating the test vote on the cryptocurrency legislation.

The University of Oklahoma led the nation in red-zone efficiency last season. The Sooners scored touchdowns more than 97% of the time when moving the ball within 20 yards of the end zone.

Ninety-seven percent is a ridiculously efficient figure. The Philadelphia Eagles were the NFL’s best red zone team last season, scoring touchdowns around 70% of the time.

The U.S. Senate is not the gridiron. But it’s clear that the bill to regulate college sports has now entered the legislative red zone. A lot of legislation gets this close to the goal line, but senators rarely enjoy the success of the Sooners or Eagles when it comes to punching it in.

That’s why it’s possible that this legislative drive could stall — despite a steady march down the field.

item.title: John Cusack stands in 'solidarity' with Mark Ruffalo amid Paramount's antisemitism allegation
item.description: John Cusack backed Mark Ruffalo after Paramount accused the actor of invoking antisemitic tropes in his criticism of Oracle's ties to the Israeli military.
item.content:encoded:
Actor John Cusack threw his support behind fellow Hollywood star Mark Ruffalo over the weekend as Ruffalo pushed back against Paramount's accusations that his criticism of tech giant Oracle invoked "antisemitic tropes."

"Solidarity — well said." Cusack wrote on X in response to Ruffalo’s lengthy defense of his remarks, which centered on Oracle’s ties to the Israeli military and the company’s leadership.

The controversy erupted after Ruffalo criticized Oracle executive vice chair Safra Catz, who also sits on Paramount’s board, and reposted a video of her discussing "really profoundly scary technologies" Oracle used to assist the Israeli military following the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas terror attacks.

CNN STAFFERS BRACE FOR PARAMOUNT CEO'S POTENTIAL PLAN TO LAUNCH EDITORIAL BOARD TO OVERSEE NETWORK

Ruffalo tied his criticism of Oracle to the Ellison family's proposed $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, pointing to Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison and his son, Paramount CEO David Ellison. The actor argued that the deal, which would put CNN, HBO and Warner Bros. under the same family's control, raises concerns about editorial independence, jobs and more.

"These 'really profoundly scary technologies' will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day used on you. Look how she revels in what we now have come to see as a genocide, which was built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle," the Marvel actor wrote in an Instagram story.

HASAN PIKER STANDS BY 'INTENTIONALLY PROVOCATIVE' CLAIMS THAT HAMAS IS 'A THOUSAND TIMES BETTER' THAN ISRAEL

Paramount subsequently issued a statement saying it was "troubled when antisemitic tropes are invoked" in what it characterized as a business dispute.

"Words like ‘genocide’ and ‘apartheid,’ applied to a corporate transaction, aren’t just wrong. They’re a bridge too far, and they cheapen the very real suffering those words are meant to describe," a company spokesperson added.

Ruffalo fired back Saturday, telling Fox News Digital the accusation that he is antisemitic was "appalling and fundamentally dishonest." He maintained that criticism of the Israeli government, military technology contracts or the executives behind them should not be equated with criticism of Jewish people.

"Scrutinizing the Ellisons, including Oracle’s business built on data, surveillance technology and government contracts and the serious threat to editorial freedom and the loss of a livelihood for thousands of families, is fair and necessary," he said.

CALIFORNIA AG ROB BONTA FACES ‘POLITICAL FAVOR’ CLAIMS OVER NETFLIX-LINKED $1M TRAIL IN PARAMOUNT SUIT

"The $111 billion deal would hand one family control over CNN, HBO and Warner Bros., backed in part by foreign money whose influence on editorial decisions has never been fully explained to the public."

"Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have called for serious national security review, and regulators still haven’t given the public a real answer. Until they do, the merger shouldn’t move forward. Now is the time to dive boldly into all these issues, not step back or concede," he added.

The potential merger has also drawn legal scrutiny from a coalition of 12 state attorneys general challenging the deal. Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery have agreed not to close the transaction until five days after a court rules on the merits of the states’ claims or June 1, 2027, whichever comes first.

In a statement noted by The Hollywood Reporter, Simon Wiesenthal Center CEO Jim Berk said, "Words matter, and so does the willingness to draw a line when legitimate debate gives way to antisemitic tropes. We commend Paramount for speaking clearly and refusing to allow prejudice to masquerade as political or corporate criticism."

Film critic Christian Toto, the founder and editor of Hollywood in Toto, told Fox News, "I'm guessing Mark would rather John Cusack have stayed silent on the matter!" Toto then pointed to controversial comments that Cusack has made on the situation in the Middle East. 

Toto continued, "More importantly, the issue in play is getting more attention now that antisemitism is flaring up in the culture at large and within the Democratic Party. That hasn't bled into Hollywood, Inc., yet, but it might sooner than later. Maybe a good example of that fracture is happening with the Paramount merger fight. Some Hollywood groups and Democrats are requesting a resolution to the matter, while others have dug their heels in, battling the merger at all costs."

He concluded, "This could get ugly, becoming a Blue on Blue battle within La La Land that could cause real damage to careers."

item.title: Marlins look to close gap in the wild card race as they host surging Red Sox in Miami tonight
item.description: Ranger Suarez takes the mound for the Boston Red Sox against Sandy Alcantara and the Miami Marlins in a crucial wild card race showdown tonight.
item.content:encoded:
We've reached the final week of August, which means there are only about four or five weeks remaining in the baseball regular season. Now is the time for teams to strap in and make their moves if they can. The postseason is within reach, and sometimes a hot team can upset the best teams. There is no guarantee the Dodgers win the World Series again, but in order to dethrone them, you need to make it to the postseason first. The Red Sox should make it, and the Marlins are still in the hunt. The two square off today in Miami.

The Boston Red Sox have been one of the hottest teams in baseball for about two months, but they did have a recent blip after all their success. They had some massive winning streaks, but over the last 16 days, the team is just 7-7. The good news for the Red Sox is that they may be entering another hot streak, having won three straight and five of their past six games. I think it is fairly unlikely they win the division, but they have a very good chance of making the postseason thanks to a 6.5-game lead over the final Wild Card spot.

Tonight, the Red Sox get one of the better off-season acquisitions taking the ball. Ranger Suarez came over from Philadelphia in the offseason and has been strong for Boston. He is just 5-3 this season, but holds a 3.41 ERA and a 1.18 WHIP. Despite missing time, he still owns 113 strikeouts for the year. He has been better on the road this season than he has been at home as well, throwing to a 2.75 ERA as a visitor compared to a 4.14 ERA when he throws at Fenway. He has struggled a bit this month, giving up eight earned runs over 13.1 innings. This might be the match-up he needs, though. He has held the Marlins hitters to just 1 hit over 21 at-bats.

The Miami Marlins are still fighting for a playoff spot, which is pretty impressive given the average age of their team. Depending on how you look at it, they are somewhere around 27 years old, so most don't have a ton of experience. The team is above .500 and is just four games back of the final playoff spot in the Wild Card race. They still need to leapfrog the Diamondbacks and Padres to own it, but they are at least in contention. That's probably more than most people would've expected this year.

RED-HOT MIAMI MARLINS CANNOT BE STOPPED, BOASTING MLB-BEST 17-5 RECORD IN MONTH OF JUNE

In an effort to try and get closer to the Padres in the race, they sent out Sandy Alcantara. It has been a bit of a bounce-back season for Alcantara as he owns a 13-8 record with a 3.46 ERA and a 1.18 WHIP. He also has 131 strikeouts for the year. Like Suarez, he has some interesting splits. In home games, he has pitched to a 2.69 ERA, but his night ERA is 4.15. Looking at his monthly performance, he has lowered his ERA every month since May, with August being his best month, allowing just four earned runs over 26 innings of work. Red Sox hitters are batting just .207 against him.

Maybe I'm a bit crazy for trying to dodge the freight train that is the Boston Red Sox, but I'm taking the Marlins tonight. Alcantara has been sharp in his action, and Suarez hasn't been quite as good. I know the Red Sox are the better team, and neither team is showing a ton of success against the opposing starter, but I like the chances of the Marlins, at home, with Alcantara on the mound, and at plus money.

item.title: Vulnerable GOP senator breaks with Trump on 2 key issues as Vance makes stop without her
item.description: Susan Collins skips JD Vance's Maine visit while opposing Trump's 50% tariffs on Canada and new postal service rules restricting mail-in voting.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, a moderate Republican seeking re-election in a blue-leaning state, is not joining Vice President JD Vance on Monday as he stops in her home state of Maine.

Collins, who at times has opposed President Donald Trump's legislative priorities, is a top target for Democrats this year as she runs in a midterm race that's among roughly a dozen that will determine if the GOP holds onto its slim Senate majority.

Vance's stop in Maine comes as Collins opposes Trump's move this past weekend to impose 50% tariffs on a range of goods from Canada, which shares a long border with Maine. And the senator is also opposed to new U.S. Postal Service rules that, if implemented, could rein in mail-in voting.

The vice president on Monday delivered remarks in Brewer, Maine, at Compotech, a defense technology manufacturer. It's the second stop this year by Vance in Maine and the second time that Collins has not teamed up with the vice president.

SUSAN COLLINS DROPS BRUTAL REMINDER OF DEMOCRAT CHALLENGER ROCKED BY ACCUSATIONS

"I am already scheduled on Monday, so I will not be able to join the vice president," Collins told reporters on Saturday.

The Senate was in session when Vance held an event in Bangor, Maine, in May, and Collins stayed in Washington. The senator holds a historic attendance record of casting over 10,000 consecutive roll call votes in the Senate dating back three decades.

But Collins, speaking to reporters as she marched in the annual Madison-Anson Days parade, her seventh parade this summer, highlighted that she teamed up last week with Energy Secretary Chris Wright when he stopped in Maine to tour a federally funded battery storage project in Lincoln built on the site of a closed paper mill.

"I really appreciated Secretary Wright's presence," Collins said.

WHAT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POLL IN MAINE'S CRUCIAL SENATE RACE SHOWS

Collins, who was one of a small group of Republicans who voted to convict Trump in a 2021 Senate trial after the House impeached him following the Jan. 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol, has at times voted against the Trump administration's wishes.

"I still think imposing new tariffs on Canada is a mistake," Collins said on Saturday.

Collins also referred to the proposed U.S. Post Office rule to implement a Trump executive order to rein in mail-in voting by refusing to deliver absentee ballots in states that have not turned over their raw voter rolls to the Justice Department or Department of Homeland Security.

"Mail-in ballots are very important to the people of Maine," Collins said. "I do no support restrictions that make it more difficult for seniors to cast votes on Election Day via the mail."

WHO'S UP AND WHO'S DOWN: CHECK OUT THE FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS ON THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS

Collins says she supports the House version of the federal SAVE America Act (Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act), which mandates documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and a photo ID for federal elections. But she joined three other Republicans and all Democrats to vote against advancing a Senate version of the bill, which is a top Trump priority.

Collins has also taken issue with the Trump administration over its crackdown on illegal immigration, and its aggressive deportation efforts. The administration received backlash following the fatal shootings by federal enforcement agents of two U.S. citizens in Minnesota who were protesting immigration operations. And the issue flared again this summer, after a fatal ICE shooting in Biddeford, Maine.

Democrats, including her Senate challenger, former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson, have repeatedly linked her to Trump, and heavily criticized her for her past funding for ICE.

Collins is the only Republican senator running for re-election in a state then-Vice President Kamala Harris carried in the 2024 election. And highlighting her differences with the president and his administration may be beneficial to Collins as she woos independent voters and even some Democrats.

Vance, during his May stop in Maine, said, "Sometimes I get frustrated with Susan Collins."

"I almost wish that she was more partisan. But the thing I love about Susan is she is independent, because Maine is an independent state. And, frankly, if she was as partisan as I sometimes wish that she was, she would not be a good fit for the people of Maine," Vance continued.

Vance added, "Let’s give a shoutout to Susan Collins, who’s doing a great job."

Vance was joined in Brewer by former two-term Republican Gov. Paul LePage, who is the GOP nominee in Maine's 2nd Congressional District.

item.title: Pilot's bravery on display in steering crippled plane clear of tragedy in dramatic water landing
item.description: Viral video captures Faith Tenkley's Piper PA-30 gliding onto the Atlantic off Boca Raton after landing gear malfunction and engine failure.
item.content:encoded:
A 23-year-old pilot’s courage in safely ditching her twin-engine Piper in the Atlantic Ocean off Boca Raton, Fla., this weekend was matched by her calm humility in a statement thanking others rather than her own heroism.

"During the descent, my primary focus was ensuring the safety of everyone around me," Faith Tenkley, 23, said in a statement to Fox News. "I was able to navigate toward open water, successfully avoiding all nearby buildings, paddleboarders and swimmers (as well as individuals using metal detectors)."

Viral video shared on social media showed the unusual and markedly smooth water landing Saturday morning as onlookers gasped; yet, video showed a man with a metal detector keenly focused on his beach treasure hunt as the stunning events unfolded around him.

FDNY DEPLOYS 140+ PERSONNEL TO JFK AFTER DELTA FLIGHT REPORTED WITH FLAT TIRES ON APPROACH TO LANDING

Tenkley, meanwhile, was dodging buildings and a busy beach while trying to find a safe way to land a crippled aircraft.

"I want to express my deepest gratitude for the concern and support following my unexpected water landing yesterday," her Sunday statement began. "I am incredibly fortunate and relieved to share that I was able to swim away from this incident.

"After deciding a landing at Boca Raton Airport was not the safest option, I continued to the coast."

Cleared by air traffic control (ATC) to land on a runway, her landing gear was malfunctioning, leaving her concerned about a hard landing with a plane still full of fuel.

FAA UNVEILS NEW AIR TRAFFIC CONTROLLER HIRING PLAN AFTER CHIEF WARNED SYSTEM WAS ‘CHRONICALLY UNDERSTAFFED’

"I want to extend my thanks to ATC for being prepared, as well as the lifeguards, firefighters and the police officers whose rapid response and professionalism ensured everyone's safety – as well as any witnesses who called for help," her statement concluded. "Thank you all for your kind messages."

Tenkley, who has been flying for four years, was the only person aboard her family’s twin-engine Piper PA-30 when it developed mechanical trouble Saturday on a flight from Page Field in Fort Myers, Florida, to Bimini in the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.

She was flying to the Bahamas to pick up her parents when the trouble began about 15 miles west of Boca Raton. She initially planned to divert to Boca Raton Airport before the plane’s landing gear malfunctioned and its right engine failed.

ARGENTINIAN FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR JUMPS TO DEATH FROM PLANE, 22-YEAR-OLD STUDENT FORCED TO LAND ALONE

As she approached the coast, Tenkley guided the disabled plane to the open stretch of water just offshore.

Video captured by a beachgoer shows the aircraft descending low over the busy Boca Raton beach before gently landing on the ocean’s surface. The Piper remained largely intact as Tenkley, wearing a bikini, swam away from the aircraft with the help of a lifeguard who arrived in moments to assist.

PILOT DECLARES MAYDAY BEFORE SEAPLANE COMES DOWN IN NEW YORK CITY’S EAST RIVER

A Boca Raton Ocean Rescue fire boat arrived shortly afterward. She was taken to a hospital as a precaution and was not reported injured.

The footage initially prompted confusion online, with some viewers mistakenly believing Tenkley was a surfer helping a male pilot. She had removed a long skirt she was wearing over her bikini to swim to shore, she told Gulf Coast News.

item.title: Browns pick Deshaun Watson as their starting QB despite home crowd booing and his '17 away games' comments
item.description: Deshaun Watson wins the Cleveland Browns quarterback competition over Shedeur Sanders, but the team makes no guarantees beyond the regular-season opener.
item.content:encoded:
It's going to be Deshaun Watson as the starting quarterback for the Cleveland Browns to open the NFL regular season, which means one thing: Get your popcorn ready because this should be entertaining.

No, not entertaining in the typical star-player-doing-amazing-things kind of way.

Entertaining in the cinema drama kind of way because what we have here is the NFL equivalent of a villain being given the opportunity to redeem himself and then deciding – by his actions – if he continues to be reviled based on what happens next.

DESHAUN WATSON BOOED BY BROWNS FANS, FIRES BACK AFTER POOR OUTING OPENS DOOR FOR SHEDEUR SANDERS

What happened Sunday evening is Browns coach Todd Monken and general manager Andrew Berry picked Watson to be their starter over Shedeur Sanders, to culminate a competition that spanned the entire offseason and into the first two preseason games.

That decision was announced to the players on Monday morning.

And now we see the next chapter of what has been the tremendously disappointing story of Watson in Cleveland. It's a story that has compounded on-field failure, Personal Conduct Policy suspension, and one injury after another the last three years.

It's a story that seemed to have a climax on Saturday when Watson was booed lustily by Browns fans – at home at Huntington Bank Field – from the moment he entered the game in the second half pretty much until the game was over.

DESHAUN WATSON'S FIRST GAME SINCE 2024 A SUCCESS BECAUSE HE WASN'T AS BAD AS SHEDEUR SANDERS OR DILLON GABRIEL

And then Watson conducted a viral press conference in which he called what Browns fans did "personal," and "disrespectful," making it seem possible that his time with the team was about to end because how does an NFL team keep a QB that gets booed at home?

Watson, indeed said, he would be playing "17 away games" if he won the starting job.

But these are the Browns, folks.

They do Browns things.

A source confirmed to OutKick the Browns did not take Watson's words into account when deciding on him as the starter.

They obviously also didn't take the booing into account.

They picked Watson over Sanders because, well, Watson is more experienced. He's more ready to face what NFL defenses will show the Browns once the season begins. A source said he was also slightly better than Sanders throughout the competition, the Saturday preseason meltdown notwithstanding.

Sanders, who had a higher completion percentage than Watson but threw one more interception, had better stay ready.

That was the coaching staff's message to the son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Deion Sanders.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Watson, you see, has been named the starter for the regular-season opener. But not for the season.

The Browns have made no guarantees to him if he plays poorly. If that happens, the team reserves the right to pivot to Sanders.

Watson has thrown 19 TD passes in his 19 games with the team, which is nowhere near what the Browns expected when they traded away six draft picks, including three first-rounders, to the Houston Texans, then signed him to a $230 million contract.

Watson has a chance to finally reward that investment to start the 2026 season. It's a small window of opportunity, but it beats the alternative for him, which was getting cut outright.

So we shall see what happens next starting with the Browns' regular-season opener, a road game at the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sept. 13.

Get your popcorn.

item.title: Alaska Senate race’s absurd name problem gets even harder to untangle
item.description: Former Anchorage Mayor Dan A. Sullivan endorses incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan over a third Dan Sullivan accused of being a Democratic plant.
item.content:encoded:
Former Anchorage Mayor Dan Sullivan is taking sides in Alaska’s unusual same-name Senate fight, endorsing incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan over a third Dan Sullivan, whose candidacy has already triggered legal challenges and allegations of an effort to confuse voters.

The intervention from Dan A. Sullivan adds another twist to a potentially competitive race in which Sen. Dan S. Sullivan and his Republican allies have accused teacher Dan J. Sullivan of running as a GOP candidate to siphon votes from the incumbent. Dan J. Sullivan has denied those accusations and says he is a legitimate moderate Republican challenger.

"As the OG Dan Sullivan, I urge Alaskans to vote for Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. He’s been great for Alaska," the former mayor wrote on social media.

DAN SULLIVAN ACCUSES SAME-NAME CHALLENGER OF TRYING TO 'RIG' ALASKA SENATE RACE

Republicans have attempted to use legal mechanisms to remove Dan J. Sullivan, who is himself running as a Republican, from the ballot. They point to the fact that he has worked with a Democratic-aligned consultant as evidence that he is part of a liberal plot to mislead voters.

Dan J. Sullivan has defended himself from the accusations by arguing that he is genuinely a moderate Republican that has real dissatisfactions with Dan S. Sullivan’s representation of the state.

It is unclear how many Dan Sullivans live in Alaska.

Alaska has a unique electoral system, something Republicans have argued could further contribute to confusion when voters head to the polls in November.

GOP SENATOR, EX-HOUSE DEM EMERGE FROM ALASKA’S ‘JUNGLE PRIMARY’ DESPITE FAR-LEFT MEDDLING

The state holds a nonpartisan primary where the top four vote-getters advance to the general election regardless of their party affiliation. Once the four candidates are chosen and Election Day arrives, Alaskans use ranked-choice voting.

Under the system, voters rank candidates in order of preference. When their first choice is eliminated, their support passes to their next choice and so on until one candidate is victorious.

Advocates of the system argue that it gives voters greater control over who ultimately wins office as well as more options to choose from. Critics, meanwhile, argue the system could cause confusion in November.

Dan S. Sullivan and Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola have advanced to the general election, though it is unclear whether Dan J. Sullivan will join them as votes are still being counted, according to the Associated Press.

JUDGE RULES REPUBLICAN WITH SAME NAME AS SEN DAN SULLIVAN CAN STAY ON ALASKA PRIMARY BALLOT

Following a Republican legal challenge, the Alaska Supreme Court held last month that Dan J. Sullivan could remain on the ballot after he was initially removed by the state’s Division of Elections. Now, federal and state prosecutors are reportedly investigating whether he is part of a conspiracy to confuse voters.

The Sullivan campaign did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Monday.

item.title: Why Wyndham Clark deserves PGA Tour Player of the Year, LIV Golf's final hoorah, and Scottie Scheffler's money
item.description: Wyndham Clark's third win of 2026 at the BMW Championship strengthens his case over Scottie Scheffler in the PGA Tour Player of the Year race.
item.content:encoded:
Wyndham Clark picked up his third win of 2026 on Sunday after flipping a switch down the stretch at the BMW Championship and fending off Rory McIlroy. With the victory, the PGA Tour Player of the Year debate has become a legitimate one for the first time in four years.

With the POY chatter at full volume, it's worth mentioning that two things can be true at once: being the best player on the planet doesn't make you the player of the year, and being the player of the year doesn't mean you're the best player on the planet. We'll get more in-depth on that down below, but spoiler: I think Clark has done plenty to end Scottie Scheffler's four-year streak of taking home POY honors.

While Clark was out playing McIlroy at Bellerive Country Club - a major championship venue - Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, and Michael La Sasso were battling at LIV Golf Indianapolis at The Club at Chatham Hills, a non-major championship venue. The potentially final chapter of LIV's story being closed out with La Sasso besting the two biggest LIV stars was certainly a scene.

Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you need to know. You can follow Mark on X @itismarkharris and email him at mark.harris@outkick.com.

The PGA Tour Player of the Year award isn't all that significant in the grand scheme of things. Approximately 99.9% of the golf world won't look back in five years and be able to name the player who took home the honors in 2026, yet that same crowd would be able to tell you who won the Masters 30 years ago.

The POY award does, however, create debate and discussion, two things we humans in sports love more than anything; therefore, we have to get into it.

Scottie Scheffler is the best golfer in the world. Nobody in their right mind would debate that statement, but that doesn't mean that he's put together the best year, and after his win at the BMW on Sunday, Clark is the one who (currently) owns that title.

Scottie Scheffler's 2026 highlights: Two wins, The American Express and the FedEx St. Jude Championship (by eight strokes), five second-place finishes, 12 total top-five finishes, lowest scoring average on the PGA Tour, zero major championship victories.

Wyndham Clark's 2026 highlights: Three wins, the CJ Cup, the U.S. Open, and the BMW Championship, six top-five finishes, one major championship victory.

Scheffler has had an incredibly strong and lucrative campaign, but Clark has him beat in the two categories we care about the most: total wins and major championships. While we can acknowledge that Scheffler's five runner-up finishes bolster his season resume, we can also admit that, even as a collective, they don't carry enough weight to trump Clark's extra victory.

If you want to play the game that Clark and Scheffler are neck-and-neck in the Player of the Year race ahead of the Tour Championship, that's perfectly fine, but only one player can win the award, and the one who hoisted a trophy at a major championship should win the theoretical tiebreaker.

LIV GOLF CEO SAYS LEAGUE IS HOPEFUL IT CAN 'DO RIGHT BY' VENDORS SUING THEM OVER ALLEGED MISSED PAYMENTS

Speaking of the Tour Championship, if Clark gets the job done in Atlanta to win back-to-back Playoff events, he would slam the door shut on the POY debate. If Scheffler, the odds-on favorite, finds the winner's circle, then we get to go through this exercise this same time next week. I'll be here.

As for Sunday's final round at the BMW Championship, it was a pillow fight between Clark and McIlroy, with Wyndham giving his five-shot lead away and looking completely out of sorts on the opening nine holes. McIlroy didn't earn any momentum really; he was more so handed it, but never grabbed hold of it.

Clark carded three consecutive birdies to close out Sunday's round to earn a three-shot victory. We'd be lying if we said it was overly exciting, but a three-shot win in a FedEx Cup Playoff event playing alongside career Grand Slam winner and fan favorite in McIlroy will always fall into the noteworthy category.

After securing his victory at Bellerive, Clark spoke about how he's one of the best players in the world. That confidence is understandably back, and he's absolutely correct in his assessment of being one of the best in the game today.

While Scheffler finished T-12 and 10 shots back of Clark at the BMW, that's not to say he didn't have a uniquely impressive week.

Following Sunday's action, he revealed he had been dealing with hand, foot, and mouth disease. Any parent to young children can attest that HFM is nasty, incredibly contagious stuff, especially if adults contract it, as it causes blisters in all three areas. Having blister-covered hands and feet while trying to play golf at the highest level seems both miserable and impossible, yet Scheffler shot four-under over the weekend to climb up the leaderboard.

With his T-12 finish at the BMW, Scheffler has earned just under $21 million this season, which is a crazy number given he's 'only' won twice. What's even more eye-opening is that the No. 2 player on this year's money list, Cameron Young, has earned $6.5 million less than Scheffler.

LIV Golf apparently has an investor in place to push the league into 2027. The emphasis on the word 'apparently' seems to be growing by the day, as only time will tell whether LIV Golf '2.0' will become a reality.

Speaking of reality, there is one where LIV Golf Indianapolis was the last LIV event the golf world ever saw. It will almost certainly be the last LIV event we see in its current form, with ginormous purses and a leaderboard with some of the game's biggest names involved.

Sunday's finish in Indianapolis was unique, with Michael La Sasso besting Jon Rahm by one shot and Bryson DeChambeau by two, but it also serves as a perfect microcosm of LIV's non-existent luster.

FRUSTRATED BUBBA WATSON CONFRONTS UNRULY FAN AT LIV GOLF INDIANAPOLIS IN INTENSE SCENE

A 22-year-old former NCAA champion from Ole Miss beating two of the best players in the world should create some sort of buzz, yet given the circumstances of the complete unknown and the fact that LIV has been on its final leg for months now, it's done virtually nothing.

The fact of the matter that will rile up the LIV Golf truthers is that if the same scenario unfolded on the PGA Tour, on a golf course people have at least heard of before, it would have been headline-worthy, at the very least.

Maybe it's oversaturation, maybe it's the fact that sports fans can only pay attention to so much. Perhaps it's the players involved or the Saudi's past-funding of the league that remains to be the biggest hold-up of interest.

I think it's more than fair to say it's a combo of all of the above, but it will be fascinating to see what unfolds with the league, and more so its players, in the coming months.

item.title: Washington Post ordered to reinstate columnist Karen Attiah after being terminated over Charlie Kirk posts
item.description: The Washington Post has been ordered to reinstate columnist Karen Attiah after being fired for Bluesky posts about Charlie Kirk's assassination.
item.content:encoded:
The Washington Post was ordered to reinstate columnist Karen Attiah after she was fired last year for social media posts she made after Charlie Kirk's assassination.

Sarah Miller Espinosa, the arbitrator overseeing Attiah's legal challenge against The Post, said the paper "did not have good and sufficient cause" and that it "violated" her labor agreement, according to The New York Times, which first reported on Espinosa's ruling last Thursday.

"The Washington Post failed to establish the grievant engaged in gross misconduct," Espinosa concluded.

TEACHERS WHO CELEBRATED CHARLIE KIRK'S ASSASSINATION NOW CASH IN WITH TAXPAYER-FUNDED SETTLEMENTS

Attiah told The Times she is "relieved to finally have that record set straight," adding, "This decision confirms what we’ve said from the start: I was doing my job as an opinion writer, and this was wrongful termination."

The columnist announced her legal victory, saying on X, "The Washington Post fired me last year for speaking the truth after Charlie Kirk's killing. I fought back. I'm happy to announce: I won my case against the Washington Post. They have been ordered to reinstate me immediately."

"In general, if someone reveals themselves to be a ghoul then companies should be able to fire them," Turning Point USA spokesman Andrew Kolvet told Fox News Digital. 

A spokesperson for The Washington Post said the paper respects the arbitration process and declined to comment further. Attiah didn't immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Attiah sparked outrage for her posts about the slain conservative icon on the liberal social media platform Bluesky.

TENNESSEE UNIVERSITY TO PAY PROFESSOR $1.9M AFTER CALLING CHARLIE KIRK A 'DISGUSTING PSYCHOPATH'

GEORGIA TEACHER RECEIVES ALMOST $300K SETTLEMENT OVER CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION POST

"Refusing to tear my clothes and smear ashes on my face in performative mourning for a White man that espoused violence is… not the same as violence," Attiah wrote at the time. In a separate post, she wrote, "Part of what keeps America so violent is the insistence that people perform care, empty goodness and absolution for White men who espouse hatred and violence.’"

Critics also slammed Attiah for misquoting Kirk in another post, attributing to him saying, "Black women do not have the brain processing power to be taken seriously. You have to go steal a White person's slot."

On a July 2023 episode of "The Charlie Kirk Show," Kirk actually said, "If we would have said three weeks ago [...] that Joy Reid and Michelle Obama, and Sheila Jackson Lee, and Ketanji Brown Jackson were affirmative-action picks, we would have been called racist. But now they're comin' out and they're saying it for us! They're comin' out, and they're saying, 'I'm only here because of affirmative action.' Yeah, we know. You do not have the brain processing power to otherwise be taken really seriously. You had to go steal a White person's slot to go be taken somewhat seriously."

Following the backlash, Attiah revealed she had been fired by The Post, saying in a termination letter her posts were "unacceptable" and "gross misconduct."

Attiah filed a legal challenge against The Post over her termination last fall, and previously announced in June that she and the paper would enter arbitration.

item.title: Arizona police shooting suspect arrested, another remains at large after killing 1, wounding fiancee

item.content:encoded:
Arizona authorities have arrested a man in connection with a home invasion shooting that killed a Tucson police recruit and left his fiancée hospitalized.

Carlos Ramirez, 23, was shot dead at his home in southwestern Tucson early Wednesday morning, according to the Pima County Sheriff's Department (PCSD). He was expected to graduate from the police academy on Aug. 27 and had previously worked for PCSD as a corrections officer. His 23-year-old fiancée, whose name has not been released, also works as a corrections officer in the department.

Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos previously said the suspects were wearing all black clothing and ski masks at the time of the shooting — which happened around 6 a.m. Wednesday.

VIDEOS SHOW THREE SUSPECTS IN SHOOTING DEATH OF TUCSON POLICE RECRUIT CARLOS RAMIREZ

Deputies arrested Santiago Jorge Rogers, 39, at a hotel on South Palo Verde Road in Tucson on Saturday morning, the sheriff said in a statement. He is being held without bond at the county jail.

Alex James Barnett, 33, remains at large. He has a rap sheet that includes prior burglary and weapons convictions and has also been known as Alex Wilson, according to court records. In December 2024, he pleaded guilty to an unlawful imprisonment charge.

According to FOX 10 Phoenix, he was last seen wearing a red shirt and black leather vest and riding a Harley-Davidson FLHXS motorcycle with the Arizona license plate, DA466.

SUSPECTS AT LARGE AFTER TUCSON POLICE RECRUIT KILLED, PIMA COUNTY CORRECTIONS OFFICER WOUNDED IN SHOOTING

A search of Pima County courts for prior cases came back empty for Rogers. However, a man of the same name and age has drug and shoplifting convictions in Yavapai County, possession of contraband behind bars in Navajo and Graham Counties, and a number of lesser charges in Prescott.

Surveillance video shows men identified as Rogers and Barnett in black clothing and picking up items at a gas station convenience store about 20 minutes before the shooting.

Hours later, surveillance video taken from a parking lot shows a third man parking the suspect vehicle, a gray Acura MDX SUV, and walking away.

He has not been publicly identified, but the sheriff's department said Sunday he had been contacted by detectives.

"No arrest has been made as investigators work to determine his involvement," the department said.

Anyone with information on the case or Barnett's whereabouts is asked to call 911 or 520-88-CRIME.

item.title: John Candy's family calls out Hollywood for weight criticism the actor endured throughout his career
item.description: Jennifer Candy-Sullivan and Rosemary Candy slam Hollywood's weight criticism of John Candy, revealing how the late comedian handled it privately.
item.content:encoded:
John Candy's family is calling out Hollywood for how their father was treated.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital at Televerse 26, the late actor's daughter, Jennifer Candy-Sullivan, and her mother, Rosemary Candy, slammed Hollywood for the way their father's weight was discussed during his fame.

"I think everyone who had some sort of difference was kind of put under a magnifying glass. So for him, it was his weight. And he kind of... he took it like a gentleman," Jennifer said. "And I think as his career went on, he was able to be more comfortable with himself and kind of vocalize and speak up for himself."

She went on to say that because of his career, people "thought he was the everyday guy and everyone loved him" so it would be okay to "pal around" and "joke around him," but that "in reality, it wasn't that okay. It's not cool."

JACK OSBOURNE FIRES BACK AT BODY SHAMERS CALLING HIM 'GROSSLY UNDERWEIGHT'

Rosemary noted that "he was able to handle it really well," but that it was still "upsetting" and "a challenge" he was dealing with early in his career, "from the beginning when I met him."

WATCH: John Candy’s daughter says actor ‘took it like a gentleman’ when Hollywood focused on his weight

Jennifer doesn't think the public or the media would be any less harsh on her father if his rise to fame occurred today, saying, "I think there would be a different type of kind of critique to him."

"I think if he tried losing weight, then it would be like, 'You're too skinny, you're no longer funny.' So I think Hollywood would find something," she said. "It would be... he doesn't... he would do something wrong. Ultimately, I think anyone in Hollywood does something wrong."

The two attended a special FYC presentation of the documentary about the comedian, "John Candy: I Like Me," as part of Televerse 26, the Television Academy festival.

The film, which originally premiered at the Toronto Film Festival in September 2025, was directed by Colin Hanks, and features interviews from many of his former co-stars, including Steve Martin, Macaulay Culkin, Bill Murray, Catherine O'Hara, Martin Short and others.

WATCH: John Candy’s daughter says Hollywood would have criticized him even if he lost weight: ‘You’re too skinny’

"When we would see John on the screen, we felt like he was one of the most relatable people," Hanks said. "And I think in working on the film and talking with people and learning more about John's past, I just felt like we didn't even understand just how relatable he was."

He explained that talking "about things like mental health and therapy" has only become popular in recent years and "wasn't something that was discussed back then." With today's lenses on, "John was even more like one of us than we even realize."

WATCH: John Candy's daughter got to see a vulnerable side of her father in the documentary 'John Candy: I Like Me'

Hanks wasn't the only one who learned something new about the "Planes, Trains and Automobiles" actor.

"I think for us, it was to see his vulnerability with those interviews. He was really good about keeping his business at work, and then family life was family life. So he tried not to bring it into the house," Jennifer said. "My mom probably understood it more because they would have conversations about it, obviously. But for us, we didn't really see it. So I think to see that on camera on the big screen was challenging."

item.title: Fla Dem Sen-nominee Angie Nixon backed abolishing Electoral College, ranked-choice voting in resurfaced clips
item.description: Resurfaced clips show Angie Nixon backing abolishing the Electoral College, ranked-choice voting, and same-day registration in her Florida Senate bid.
item.content:encoded:
Resurfaced clips show Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon supporting abolishing the Electoral College, embracing ranked-choice voting and allowing voters to register on Election Day in a series of comments Republicans are seizing on as the democratic socialist begins her general-election campaign.

In one March 14 clip with the Clay County Speaks podcast, Nixon was asked about eliminating the Electoral College.

"Abolish the Electoral College, I’m fine with that," Nixon said. "I believe one vote, one person. We would have a different country right now if that was the case."

She then supported abolishing the Senate filibuster, which gives the minority party a block on the majority's agenda.

5 TAKEAWAYS FROM FLORIDA SENATE PRIMARY: GOP SEN ASHLEY MOODY WILL FACE DSA'S NIXON

Nixon also rejected nonparty voters participating in Democratic primary elections, saying it "marginalizes" the voter’s voice — echoing a rationale historically advanced for the Electoral College's protecting smaller states from being drowned out by more populous ones.

Asked separately about ranked-choice voting, Nixon responded, "I’m totally fine with that."

Nixon expressed the same positions publicly during a June online question-and-answer session with voters.

WATCH: DEMOCRATS ADMIT WHEN THEY'D ELIMINATE THE FILIBUSTER AS SAVE ACT FIGHT HEATS UP

On the same Clay County Speaks podcast, Nixon also advocated same-day voter registration.

"I also believe that," she said, "you can register same day and vote that day."

Florida currently closes voter registration ahead of Election Day rather than permitting voters to register at the polls.

WHO IS ANGIE NIXON? BULLHORN-WIELDING SOCIALIST UPSETS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE IN SUNSHINE STATE STUNNER

"Far-left socialist Angie Nixon isn’t running to protect our elections — she’s running to dismantle them," RNC Election Integrity Communications Director Ally Triolo told Fox News Digital in a statement. "From abolishing the Electoral College and embracing ranked-choice voting to attacking voter ID and commonsense election safeguards, Nixon’s radical agenda is a direct threat to American election security. Anyone determined to tear down this sacred pillar of our nation is unfit for public office."

Fox News Digital reached out to Nixon's Florida state representative's office and her campaign for comments and an interview, but they did not immediately respond.

Nixon, a Florida state representative and member of the Democratic Socialists of America, stunned the Democratic establishment last week when she defeated heavily funded former national security official Alexander Vindman for the party’s U.S. Senate nomination. She will face Republican Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., in November.

The RNC is rebuking Nixon's views about how elections should be run as the Jacksonville Democrat makes the jump from the state legislature to a campaign that is expected to draw national attention and potentially big dollars from Democrats in a bid to flip the Senate majority this November.

CARVILLE TELLS DEMOCRATS TO 'JUST QUIT FIGHTING' AGAINST VOTER ID REQUIREMENTS, WARNS IT POLLS AT 75%

Nixon has also sharply criticized election integrity measures enacted by Florida Republicans under Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis.

A 2021 law signed by DeSantis shortened the duration of standing vote-by-mail requests, required voters to provide additional identifying information when requesting ballots and placed new restrictions on ballot drop boxes and third-party ballot collection. Republicans enacted additional mail-voting requirements in 2023.

The fight comes as voter identification requirements continue to draw overwhelming support nationally, despite the Senate failing to move the Save America Act that requires voter ID nationwide.

A Fox News poll conducted July 17–20 found 83% of registered voters supported requiring photo identification to register to vote, while 77% backed requiring photo ID to cast a ballot. Support crossed party lines, including 72% of Democrats who supported an ID requirement for registration and 62% who supported one for voting.

FOX NEWS POLL: SIGNIFICANT SUPPORT FOR BOTH VOTER ID LAWS AND MAIL-IN BALLOTS

Nixon’s rhetoric has extended beyond election rules to Republican officials and the state’s judicial system.

"What it’s going to take is voting these fascists out of office," Nixon said, repeatedly applying that label to Florida DeSantis.

"We have a governor that continually cheats," Nixon told a podcast in 2024. "At the end of the day, he’s a fascist, he’s a dictator."

Nixon also accused Florida courts of protecting DeSantis and his political allies because of the governor’s role in judicial appointments.

DAVID MARCUS: WHY DEMOCRATS' HAREBRAINED POPULAR VOTE SCHEME MIGHT BACKFIRE

"When you have courts that have been chosen by a fascist, of course they’re gonna look out for the fascists," she told that same podcast.

Nixon now faces Moody in the Nov. 3 special election for the Senate seat formerly held by Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

item.title: Sam Burns is one of America's best golfers, but faith, family and the USA matter more to him than golf
item.description: Sam Burns told OutKick his son Bear will experience the Presidents Cup at Medinah with him as the five-time PGA Tour winner earns his fifth Team USA spot.
item.content:encoded:
Sam Burns is headed back to represent the United States.

Again.

Burns officially clinched an automatic spot on the U.S. Presidents Cup team Sunday, giving the 30-year-old his third Presidents Cup appearance and fifth consecutive Team USA appearance across the Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup.

EXCLUSIVE: SAM BURNS WANTS LIV GOLF STARS JON RAHM, BRYSON DECHAMBEAU BACK ON THE PGA TOUR

If you're a diehard golf fan, none of that is particularly surprising.

Burns first represented the United States at the Junior Ryder Cup when he was 18 years old. More than a decade later, he's a five-time PGA Tour winner, one of the best American golfers in the world and a fixture on U.S. teams.

But this time, something is different.

His son is going to experience it with him.

"Bear this year, he'll be around the team and get to hang out and really enjoy it," Burns told OutKick in an exclusive interview on Aug. 18.

Burns and his wife, Caroline, welcomed Bear in April 2024. Their daughter, Belle, arrived on July 3.

Bear is only 2, so he’s still too young to understand what his dad is doing when he represents the United States. Burns knows his children won't fully comprehend what their dad has accomplished for quite some time.

LSU ALUM SAM BURNS MAKES IT CLEAR HIS SON WAS NOT NAMED AFTER BEAR BRYANT

But they're going to grow up watching him wear USA on his chest, and that clearly means something to Burns.

"It is such an honor for me to be able to represent your country and also play for ultimately something a lot bigger than yourself," Burns said. "And you have teammates that week that you're playing for and their families."

Golf is about as individual as sports get.

Most weeks, Burns is trying to beat everyone else in the field.

For a few weeks throughout his career, he's been playing for something else.

"It's such a special week," Burns said. "And it's a week that I think most guys, when they look back on their career, when it's over, those will be the weeks that they remember."

Casual sports fans might not immediately put his name alongside the biggest stars in golf, but his résumé is getting increasingly difficult to overlook.

Burns has won five times on the PGA Tour, though he hasn't won since 2023. This summer, he came painfully close to winning his first major championship, finishing second at the U.S. Open and third at The Open.

Burns held the 54-hole lead at Royal Birkdale last month before ultimately finishing two shots behind winner Ryan Fox.

He played in the final pairing at the FedEx St. Jude Championship alongside world No. 1 and close friend Scottie Scheffler last weekend. Scheffler ultimately hoisted the trophy, but Burns locked up another top-five finish, his fourth of the 2026 season.

All of that makes him one of the best American golfers casual sports fans might not know, and golf isn't even the most important thing in his life.

Not even close.

Burns spoke with OutKick at The Highlands Golf & Tennis in St. Louis, where he partnered with Raising Cane's to work with local kids ahead of the BMW Championship.

The 30-year-old is now a father of two, and OutKick asked him what becoming a dad has taught him about himself.

"I think you don't realize how impatient you are until you have kids," Burns said.

He talked about trying to reason with a toddler or newborn who doesn't understand what Dad is trying to explain. But then Burns got to the part of fatherhood that seems to have changed his perspective the most.

"You feel like they may be an inconvenience at times and then you just realize they want your attention and they want your love," Burns said. "So it's really special to be a dad for sure."

GOLF STAR BRYSON DECHAMBEAU OPENS UP ABOUT WANTING FOUR KIDS AND HOW HE THINKS FAMILIES SHOULD WORK

Burns has already had to put those priorities into practice this year.

Earlier this summer, he was prepared to miss The Open because Caroline was due to give birth around the same time.

Belle arrived early, 13 days before the first round of The Open, and Caroline ultimately encouraged her husband to make the trip to Royal Birkdale.

He went and nearly won the tournament.

This isn't someone using "golf isn't everything" as an excuse for being indifferent about golf.

He's an elite professional athlete who wants to win. He puts an enormous amount of time into trying to become better and has spent this season coming extremely close to one of the few accomplishments still missing from his résumé: a major championship.

But Burns has also spoken openly about his Christian faith and his belief that golf is what he does, not who he is.

Saying that is one thing. Maintaining that perspective while trying to beat the best golfers in the world is another.

OutKick asked Burns if he could remember a moment when golf truly tested his faith.

"Every day," he said.

Anyone who has ever picked up a club knows golf has a way of doing that.

"You put so many hours and so much effort into something, and a lot of the times you don't really see the results right away," Burns said. "You can hit really good shots and end up in bad places, or bad shots end up in good places. Sometimes it seems silly, but ultimately it's a game that teaches you a lot about life and definitely can make you realize what's most important."

For Burns, the perspective comes back to three things: faith, family and country.

Golf matters to him, obviously.

Burns didn't become a five-time PGA Tour winner, contend for major championships and earn five consecutive Team USA spots without pouring himself into the game.

But Burns also seems to understand the distinction between caring deeply about something and allowing it to define you.

When Burns heads to Medinah next month, not only will he be there representing the United States, but his son Bear will be there to start watching him do it.

Burns has plenty of golf left, and plenty of time to add to an already impressive résumé. A major championship remains out there. So do more PGA Tour wins and, presumably, more opportunities to wear the red, white and blue.

But when Burns eventually looks back on all of it, he already has a pretty good idea which weeks will stand out.

The ones when he was playing for something bigger than himself.

item.title: Birth tourism scams draw sweeping crackdown as visa revocations climb
item.description: The State Department's new Birth Tourism and Prevention Task Force has already revoked more than 750 visas as officials track travel patterns worldwide.
item.content:encoded:
The State Department is cracking down on a popular form of visa fraud through a sophisticated worldwide operation that has already revoked hundreds of visas.

The department's spokesman, Tommy Pigott, told Fox News Digital that under the direction of President Donald Trump, the American government is partnering with agencies across the globe to halt the practice of birth tourism.

Birth tourism refers to travel to the United States for the primary purpose of giving birth so a child can obtain U.S. citizenship. The practice has been linked to visa-fraud schemes in which applicants conceal or misrepresent the purpose of their travel, often while seeking entry on visitor visas. A U.S.-citizen child may also create future immigration options for family members, including the ability to petition for a parent after turning 21.

TRUMP SIGNS EXECUTIVE ORDERS TARGETING BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP, BIRTH TOURISM AFTER SUPREME COURT SETBACK

It has also become a for-profit industry, where facilitators of the fraud market their services for helping women break America's laws through "birth in the U.S." services, including arranging visa scams to get women into the country.

"The first step in that is identifying them," Pigott said. "We have consular officers around the world that work with international partners, that work for law enforcement officials to identify patterns that indicate a birth tourism network, and then when that is identified, we take actions such as revoking their visas, which was the recent announcement that we made, to make sure that we're dismantling those networks."

ABBOTT ORDERS PROBE AFTER TEXAS HOSPITAL ADVERTISES 'BIRTH PACKAGES' IN MEXICO: 'CITIZENSHIP IS NOT FOR SALE'

Earlier this month, the State Department announced that it was launching a Birth Tourism and Prevention Task Force.

"We're making adjustments because it's very unfair," Trump said. "They're building businesses around birthright citizenship. That's not the way it was supposed to work. It's a disgrace. They're buying their way in, and we're not going to let it happen."

Through the task force, government officials are now analyzing in real time travel trends by visa holders around the world that are indicative of the practice.

TEXAS GOV ABBOTT SIGNS EXECUTIVE ORDER CRACKING DOWN ON 'BIRTH TOURISM,’ SAYS US CITIZENSHIP NOT FOR SALE

In one recent case, a woman who came to the United States on a tourist visa under the impetus of a weeks-long vacation, continuously received visits from her partner, who lived outside the country. That pattern raised officials' suspicions, who understood the partner's movements as visits to the United States to support the woman in the latter stages of her pregnancy and possibly present in the country during the child's birth.

"That was an indication that this was actually a birth tourism effort here, and we were able to take action to revoke those visas," said Pigott. "So we're able to analyze those travel patterns, analyze those instances that indicate fraud, look into those, and the task force we have allows us to take that action.

Pigott provided some examples of the blatant fraud.

BIRTH TOURISM COULD SOON CARRY A SEVERE NEW CONSEQUENCE FEW WOULD RISK: 'EXISTENTIAL CRISIS'

"There were some advertisements that were being published talking about a world without borders or automatic guaranteed citizenship in their advertisements while they were pretending to offer health care services," he said. "In reality, that is fraud, and the fraud actually doesn't just end when it has to do with the birth tourism example of lying to the consular officer."

"These networks are set up in the United States and then further coach these individuals on how to not pay their medical bills," he continued. "So you have fraud when you enter the United States and then the American taxpayer is left footing the bill. It comes down to the fundamental principle: we're gonna protect the sacred privilege of American citizenship and not allow this fraud to happen."

TRUMP DOJ UNLEASHES LARGEST DENATURALIZATION EFFORT IN DEPARTMENT HISTORY — AND SAYS IT’S ‘ONLY THE BEGINNING’

The task force, officially launched on Aug. 12, has already revoked more than 750 visas tied to suspected birth-tourism activity. The State Department expects that number to increase dramatically in a very short period of time.

Pigott added that under the Trump administration, visa security is an important part of a much broader overall effort to secure the border, adding that the Biden administration, "did everything they could to allow for the abuse of our legal immigration system and allowed for the unprecedented border crisis that we saw."

Under President Joe Biden, an estimated 10 million people crossed the border into the United States illegally.

item.title: 'Harry Potter' star Jessie Cave felt 'it was embarrassing' turning to OnlyFans amid money struggles
item.description: "Harry Potter" actress Jessie Cave reveals the desperate financial moment that pushed her to join OnlyFans, where she now posts non-explicit hair videos.
item.content:encoded:
"Harry Potter" star Jessie Cave admitted she felt embarrassed about joining OnlyFans after struggling to support her four children despite appearing in the blockbuster film franchise.

During a Thursday appearance on ITV's "This Morning," Cave, who played Lavender Brown in the "Harry Potter" movies, said she faced financial pressure while raising four children and navigating an unpredictable acting career before joining the subscription-based platform.

"I was in Harry Potter, but it was a smallish part, and it was 20 years ago. I've done little roles ever since, and I've mainly done comedy," Cave said.

FORMER NICKELODEON CHILD STAR REVEALS HIDDEN PRICE OF FAME AFTER SHARING RESIDUAL CHECKS WORTH PENNIES

"People just assume I'm rich, and I have loads of money, and no, I don't," she continued. "So it was embarrassing because, on a certain level, I would have really liked to get a job. But you know what it's like, you have kids. It costs so much for childcare."

Cave launched her account in March 2025 to post videos of herself brushing, braiding and styling her waist-length hair. She has described the content as catering to a niche audience with an interest or "fetish" in hair.

SCARLETT JOHANSSON, WHO EARNED $43 MILLION IN 2025, SAYS LIFE IS A CONSTANT 'DEFICIT' AT HOME

Cave said raising four children made it increasingly difficult to afford acting and live performances.

"I mean even going to the Edinburgh Festival, I can't even really afford to do the whole run anymore, because I can't afford how much it would cost to take all my kids," she said. "And people assume 'Oh don't take your kids,' but I want to take my kids."

GOLDEN GLOBE WINNER ANN JILLIAN LEFT HOLLYWOOD AT HER PEAK FOR MOTHERHOOD: ‘SOMETHING IS GOING TO SUFFER’

"I have felt like I've had to apologize a lot," Cave continued. "I think it's a choice to have four kids as well. I've always wanted to make art at the same time, and also, I chose to do this weird job."

"I couldn't really have done anything else. ... I have managed to keep afloat workwise as an actress. It's a very small proportion of people who work regularly," she noted.

‘AMERICAN PIE’ ALUM SHANNON ELIZABETH TURNS TO ONLYFANS FOR ‘FRESH START’ AS DIVORCE UNFOLDS

"And I have done the odd job here, and I have managed to keep afloat for 18 years, and it just came to a moment a couple of years ago where I was like 'Oh yeah, I don't really know what I would do' and this was an option. I'm now so glad, I'm so glad."

Cave previously discussed her OnlyFans career in an interview with The Times and revealed how much she had earned from the platform. She said she had "earned more, easily, than my entire acting career within one year."

JAIME PRESSLY ADMITS SHE THOUGHT ONLYFANS WAS 'PORN' BEFORE HER SURPRISE DEBUT ON THE PLATFORM

"I thought I’d make five grand, be on it for a few months, and it would buy me time to work out what we’re going to do," Cave said. "But it’s now been over a year and a half, and it’s genuinely saved our lives."

Cave charges subscribers $6 a month for her non-explicit "hair content," which includes videos of her brushing her hair while fully clothed and dressed in costumes, braiding it and tying it into a ponytail.

'KNOTS LANDING' ICON DONNA MILLS JOINS ONLYFANS AT 85 TO CONNECT WITH FANS 'ON HER OWN TERMS’

Cave said singers Lily Allen and Kate Nash inspired her to join OnlyFans after they launched their own pages on the platform.

Although she described motherhood as the most important part of her life, Cave said she had made a conscious decision not to share photos or information about her children on social media.

‘AMERICAN PIE’ STAR SHANNON ELIZABETH SWEARS OFF DATING, SAYS ONLYFANS IS ‘THE ONLY RELATIONSHIP I NEED’

"I don't really post much about my kids," she said on "This Morning." "... I didn't want to post them, so I just started doing funny videos of me brushing my hair and plaiting my hair. And then people liked them, and I thought, just, 'Oh' and I was really in a quite desperate spot. And at the time, Lily Allen had just come on. She'd said she'd used her feet for money, and I thought this sounds great!"

"Kate Nash has funded her tours with doing it. I just thought, ‘I mainly do one-woman shows with puppets’," Cave continued. "Yes, I was in 'Harry Potter' but I'm a struggling artist basically."

‘X-FILES’ STAR GILLIAN ANDERSON REVEALS PARENTING REGRET, SAYS SHE WISHES SHE WAS 'LESS SELFISH'

"I took a chance, and I thought I'd make a little bit of money to fund, or to pay back the money I lost during one of the Edinburgh Festivals I've done, because it's extortionate now, and I've just kept going," she shared. "I kind of now think of it, I mean it's not art but it's artful. It's really long, my hair, so you can do a lot with it. I do all sorts. I kind of think of it like a circus act now."
